_comment: Shepherd. Long hours, few people, and animals that are not pets.
The §12.4 anchors are the flock, lambing, the dog, the high pasture, shearing and predators. These
three take a lambing that is going badly, a dog getting too old for the hill, and a stretch of
fence nobody will help her mend.
The shepherd's voice is shaped by solitude: she talks in long, unhurried sentences because she has
had nobody to interrupt her, and she is matter-of-fact about death in a way that startles people
who keep chickens and think they understand.
